name: Archaeological Area and the Patriarchal Basilica of Aquileia
description: Aquileia, in Italy's northeastern Friuli-Venezia Giulia region near the head of the Adriatic, was founded as a Roman colony in 181 BC and grew into a city of perhaps 100,000 people before Attila's army sacked it in the 5th century. Much of it still lies buried under farmland. Its basilica, famed for a vast early mosaic floor, helped spread Christianity into central Europe.
